content.title: The Path to Peace — Negotiations at City Point
content.description: On a riverboat near Petersburg, Lincoln and Confederate Vice President Stephens meet to discuss peace. The war is winding down. Lincoln desires rapid reunion with minimal punishment.

choices.text: Offer generous reunion terms: quick readmission, limited punishment.
choices.costDescription: Satisfies few Republicans; risks political backlash
choices.consequence: Lincoln offers generous terms. The Confederacy hesitates. Radical Republicans explode in protest. The moment passes. Fighting continues. Lee refuses surrender on moderate terms.

choices.text: Demand unconditional surrender with Reconstruction terms.
choices.consequence: You demand unconditional surrender. The Confederacy refuses. Lee marches toward Appomattox. Three weeks of desperate retreat follow. Lee surrenders when escape becomes impossible.

comments: Reviewed and declined for mainline integration.
review_note: Rejected because the current Appomattox / Greensboro ending model is historically stronger and this draft duplicated the peace-ending slot with weaker causal logic.
